prompt:
I need the front end for Curbrota. Scheduling software used by a mid-sized city's Office of Small Business to assign licensed food trucks to the city's curbside vending zones week by week, and to work around trucks' availability, street closures and special events.

Who's using it: Marisol Achebe, a permit coordinator in the city's Office of Small Business. She has run the vending rotation for three years, knows most truck owners by name, and answers to a program manager and to city council members who get complaints about crowded or empty curbs.

What they're doing right now: It is Monday morning and she is building the December rotation, which goes out to vendors Friday. Over the weekend six trucks sent back their December availability forms, two owners asked to swap their Saturday zones, and Public Works just announced that Fifth Street will be closed December 8–12 for water main work, which wipes out the Courthouse zone for that week. The Winter Lights market on December 13–14 also takes over the Riverside zones. She has to move the displaced trucks, keep every truck at or near its guaranteed four slots for the month, honor the fairness rule that no truck gets the high-traffic Civic Plaza zone more than twice a month, and spot any days when a zone would be left empty.

What's in the system at this point: 14 curbside vending zones, each with a name (Civic Plaza, Courthouse, Riverside North, Riverside South, Medical District, University Ave, and others), a capacity of 1–3 trucks, allowed hours (e.g. 10:30–15:00 weekdays; 17:00–22:00 Fri–Sat for the nightlife zones), and a traffic tier from A to C. 62 licensed trucks, each with an owner, a cuisine, permit number and expiry (3 expire in December), a monthly slot guarantee (4 for standard permits, 8 for premium), and December availability (available, partial with listed days, or not operating; 9 trucks have not returned forms). A proposed December grid of 31 days × zones with about 310 slot assignments, 23 of them currently conflicting with the Fifth Street closure or the Winter Lights footprint. 2 pending swap requests between named trucks. Last month's actual attendance: 4 no-shows logged, 1 truck on a warning. City holidays: December 24 afternoon and December 25 closed.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
